drift.far: Somewhere far off on the ice, a dull crack and groan
drift.moved: The floe shifted. A polynya opened between the floes
drift.ridge: The ice closed in: a hummocky ridge rose
drift.warn: The ice creaks underfoot: the floe will move!
fact.CANVAS_x: Canvas: tinder for fire, the base of a torch and rope. It blocks the wind only half as well.
fact.COAL_x: Coal burns twice as long as driftwood. Sacks lie in the mine shafts and carts: there is no need to dig it out of the wall.
fact.DIRT_x: Permafrost: in summer it thaws a hand's depth; in winter it is harder than stone. Can be dug with a shovel, but slowly.
fact.GLASS_x: Glass barely holds heat, but lets light through.
fact.GRAVEL_x: Gravel runs like sand and can be dug with a shovel. In a cave-in it is mixed with beams; stone sticks out from under it.
fact.HARDROCK_x: Granite is denser than stone: it takes long to break and only a pickaxe will do. The cape's hills are made of it.
fact.ICE_x: Ice conducts heat ten times better than snow and gives no warmth. But it is clear, melts into water twice as efficiently as snow, and sea ice thicker than a man is tall cannot be broken by hand.
fact.LICHEN_x: Reindeer moss: dry, it catches fire at once. The best tinder and bedding under hides.
fact.LOG_x: Driftwood, timber supports and planks: dry wood burns long. Supports hold up the roof: knock out a post and the ceiling sinks.
fact.METAL_x: Iron pulls heat from the hand: don't touch it with bare skin. Used for ice chisels and points.
fact.PACKED_x: Packed snow: snow compressed by wind or time. It is denser and stronger; 250–380 kg/m³ makes the best blocks.
fact.PLANK_x: Planks: house frame, flooring and beams. They burn twice as fast as logs.
fact.SNOWBLOCK_x: A placed block sinters in 25–60 minutes and fuses with the wall; until it has fused, it is weaker. A wall two blocks thick holds the lamp's heat.
fact.SNOW_x: Loose snow, 60–150 kg/m³: it holds more air than ice. It keeps heat but can't bear loads: a roof of it will collapse, and a knife won't cut a block from it.
fact.SOAPSTONE_x: Soft and greasy to the touch, it does not crack from fire: fat lamps are made from it.
fact.STONE_x: Stone holds anything, but heat leaves it fast. It can't be taken by hand: you need a pickaxe. Fox-proof caches are built from it.
fact.WATER_x: Water does not freeze until −1.9 °C. If you fall in, you have about 20 seconds to get out before cold shock sets in. Wet in the frost is more dangerous than the cold.
fact.WHALEBONE_x: Light and strong: it spans a gap where wood would sag. Chopped with an axe.
fact.WOOD_x: Wood washed up by the sea: dry, and the salt keeps it from rotting. The main winter fuel.
fact.iceThin_x: New ice over a polynya is thinner than two palms. It cracks underfoot; the ice chisel will show its thickness.
fact.none: Nothing yet. Walk the world and look at snow, ice and stone: everything you study for a while is recorded here.
fact.snowDense_x: Above 420 kg/m³: the block comes out heavy, sharp-edged and insulates worse. Fine for walls, but hard to carry.
fact.snowGood_x: 250–380 kg/m³: cuts with a knife, lays flat and holds a vault. The warmest material on the cape.
fact.snowLoose_h: Loose snow: the knife is useless
fact.snowLoose_x: Below 220 kg/m³ a block crumbles in your hands. Look for packed snow in the lee, under a drift or by the ridge.

itemdesc.axe: Chops wood and bone: driftwood, logs, props, whale ribs.
itemdesc.bandage: Binds a frostbitten hand, foot or face. If there is alcohol in the bag, it is used to treat the wound first.
itemdesc.belt_pouch: Carry it: adds three quick slots on your belt (keys 7, 8, 9).
itemdesc.big_pack: Carry it: six extra slots and 20 more kg of load. But you sweat 20% more.
itemdesc.binoculars: Hold LMB: the camera looks twice as far. When there is light (moon, aurora, twilight), animal marks are visible at long range.
itemdesc.compass: The needle points to the target: station, schooner, signal hill, smoke and your marks. Press to switch to the next target. Hold 0.6 s to mark this spot. Works in a blizzard too.
itemdesc.fishing_line: For a hole or polynya. Bare fingers freeze.
itemdesc.flask: Keeps water warm inside your coat.
itemdesc.frost_balm: Rub on hands and face before going out in the cold: frostbite progresses 40% slower for about two hours. Enough for four uses.
itemdesc.hand_warmer: A tin box with live coal. Carry it: hands and face freeze more slowly, and hands warm up. Burns for about four hours. To light: coal and fire nearby.
itemdesc.harpoon: For a seal at the hole: strike when it surfaces.
itemdesc.ice: Sea ice: melts into water better than snow.
itemdesc.ice_chisel: Works on ice: holes, ice blocks, thickness of the ice underfoot.
itemdesc.ice_cleats: Spikes for boots. Grip on bare ice, slip on wind-polished ice, sink in loose snow. Need boots or felt boots.
itemdesc.pick: Breaks stone and ice plugs. Ill-suited for soil and snow.
itemdesc.probe_pole: Jab the snow in front of you: it shows ice thickness, polynyas and voids under the snow up to six steps ahead. Made from driftwood and rope.
itemdesc.sack: Loose items, 12 pieces to a spot, half the weight: snow, ice, coal, lichen. Wet snow in the sack soaks your clothes.
itemdesc.saw: Faster than an axe on logs and planks, faster than a knife on snow blocks.
itemdesc.shovel: Moves snow: scoop, throw, tamp down, bury.
itemdesc.sled: Pull it behind you: +30 slots. Use it to harness up.
itemdesc.smoke_flare: Thick smoke for three minutes: visible from afar by day and at twilight. The icebreaker takes it as a signal, like a flare.
itemdesc.snow: Loose snow from the shovel. In a pot, it becomes water.
itemdesc.snow_block: Cut with a snow knife. The denser it is, the heavier and stronger.
itemdesc.snow_goggles: A slit instead of lenses. Protects the eyes from blinding snow and cuts the wind and drift. Worn on the face.
itemdesc.snow_knife: Cuts snow blocks from dense packed snow. Loose snow crumbles.
itemdesc.sonde_balloon: A meteorological balloon. On the sonde pad it is tied to the radiosonde with a rope.
itemdesc.sonde_probe: A box with pressure and wind sensors. It goes into the sky on the balloon.
itemdesc.spirit: For treating frostbite together with a bandage. If you drink it: you feel warm, but the body cools.
itemdesc.tea: Dry tea. Brewed in a pot.
itemdesc.thermos: Hot water or tea for three sips. Keeps heat for about six hours. Fill it by a fire, kettle or pot.
itemdesc.torch: Burns about an hour. Lights a mine shaft and scares off animals.
itemdesc.whistle: Blow it: Sever comes running and follows you. Hold it: let him wait in place.

mine.creak: The frozen roof creaks. It rests on two props: don't knock out both.
mine.sag: The roof sagged: one prop no longer holds. Don't touch the second!
note.n10_x: If you fall through a hole, don't shake yourself off. Get out onto dry snow and roll: the powder draws water out of the fur like blotting paper. Then to the fire. Foma ran to the ship wet and never made it. Don't run wet.
note.n11_x: The sled was built from deck boards: four planks, two bones, straps. With a sled one man hauls the load of three. But the ice does not like hurry: before a lead, test with the ice chisel that it is thicker than a man is tall.
note.n12_x: December. The captain ordered the stove fed with frames: we no longer need the ship. Kupriyanov argued that burning the ship is burning the house, and went ashore with nine men, with lamps and fat, to build snow houses. I stayed: aboard it is warm and fed.
note.n13_x: January. The ship's timber ran out by midnight; the stove went cold and there is no fat left. Ryndin lost three fingers. From the deck I see the smoke of Kupriyanov's lamp on the shore, thin as a thread and steady. They are alive. We burned boards and froze. They guarded the fire, and they live.
note.n14_x: February. I'm going out to them while I can still walk. I leave the diary on deck. If you read this, remember: never let the fire go out, snow is shelter, fat is life. Warmth is not where there is much firewood, but where there are few holes. Velsky.
note.n1_t: Page 1 · Tin can by the cairn
note.n1_x: 12 September. The «Zarya» froze into the ice four versts from this cape. I am building a cairn and leaving this page in the tin: whoever finds it, take it. The musher showed me the lamp used to warm snow houses: a flat stone, fat, a wick of lichen. A fire the size of a fingernail, and the house is warm. Remember: the lamp is the heart of the house.
note.n2_x: October. The miners left, leaving the timber supports, carts and sacks of coal. In the gallery it is dark as a sack; a smoked torch helps: driftwood, a drop of fat and a scrap of canvas. We found a pickaxe at the portal: don't leave it. Ahead is a cave-in, and the stone there can't be taken by hand.
note.n3_x: In the hut it is warm from the old stove. I dry mittens on poles over the fire: wet in the frost is worse than the frost itself. Two poles and a rope are the whole drying rack; by the fire, things dry twice as fast. Wet fur on the body freezes like tin.
note.n4_x: A hide bed laid over lichen warms from below: ice under the back is the main thief of heat. Until there is a door, we hang a seal-hide flap over the entrance: in hard frost it blocks half the wind. On top, snow, and the draft is gone.
note.n5_x: The hut stands on two log props, left and right. In winter they are frozen like stone and they creak, so they are working. Above us is not rock but gravel on boards. Look for driftwood on the shore, and don't touch the props.
note.n6_x: An arctic fox carried off a ham from an open sack overnight and left as calmly as if it were its own house. Now we hide supplies under stones: six boulders, and the fox can't get them. For ptarmigan we set snares: a rope and a twig, on the tundra by the lichen.
note.n7_x: By the whale skeleton the musher sews: mittens from hide, kamiks from two hides, thread of sinew. Wear only dry things: the trick is keeping the hand from sweating. Fine work. Fingers lose feeling in minutes in the cold, so sew by the fire or in a house.
note.n8_x: We fish by the crack. Line: a bone hook and sinew. The fish bites when you don't make noise. Sinew comes from the seal: it is butchered quickly, before it cools. Meat, fat, skin, sinew. Sinew makes thread and line; only what goes unnoticed is lost.
note.n9_x: The iceberg is hollow as a shell: no wind inside at all, and the light through the wall is blue. We slept three together; the ice holds the lamp's heat. Only at night the wall sweats and drips, so lay down hides. Parkas are sewn like this: three hides, two arctic foxes, a heavier thread. Sew only in warmth.
note.s1_x: Entry 41. The radio died before night: the lamp and coil burned out, and the battery went flat. Better not to think about that for now. Warmth and fat first. I'm going to the holes with a harpoon: a bone from the beach, from the whale, driftwood, rope and a piece of iron for the tip. I'm tying it on the table in the house: by the stove the hands don't freeze.
note.s2_x: Entry 44. I took the triode lamp to the schooner to warm it in the cabin, where the stove is. Fool: the ice moved off and I couldn't carry it back. The coil stayed in the miners' hut; the battery is under a drift in the diesel shed. The antenna mast was torn down; set it up again: three planks (or a bone) and two ropes. Without the mast, the radio is just a box.
note.s3_x: Entry 46. I don't heat the house with diesel: fumes. But an empty drum, if you knock out the bottom with an axe, can be stuffed with driftwood and set up as a brazier. It warms like a stove, only with more smoke. I cut holes with the ice chisel: two iron bits and driftwood on a shaft. The ice is thicker than a man is tall, so you can't reach through it by hand.

rad.echo1: Through the noise, very far off: «…never let the fire go out… snow is shelter, fat is life…»
rad.echo2: «…the lamp's smoke thin as a thread and steady… they are alive…»
rad.echo4: «…I'm coming out to you. If you hear this, get warm, don't hurry… Velsky…»
rad.echoDay: The ether is dead: this voice doesn't come through in daylight

rad.hint: Three stations are marked on the scale. Hold the needle on the mark until you catch it.
rad.hintNight: By day the ether is dead: only static. Better to listen at night.
rad.hintRadio: Radio: the receiver runs on the generator. Meteo gives an accurate forecast for a day; at night, other voices come through too.
rad.hintSonde: Weather sonde: balloon + radiosonde + rope. Launch the sonde and you get an accurate forecast and see ice cracks for a day.
rad.iceEta: «Expect them in {d}. Hold on, light the signal fire on the cape's hill.»
rad.iceHere: «The icebreaker is in sight of the shore. Fire on the hill, immediately!»
rad.iceNo1: «Murmansk Radio calling «Cape of Silence». We don't hear you…»
rad.iceNo2: «…Repeat, do you hear. The station's transmitter is not answering…»
rad.iceYes1: «Murmansk Radio: your signal received. The icebreaker has reached the cape.»
rad.jEcho: Radio at night: a voice from the 1890s, like a recording in the ice. «Never let the fire go out».
rad.jIce: Radio: the icebreaker's dispatcher on the line. The station's transmitter is still silent.
rad.jNum: Radio: on the number frequency they read the keeper's log entries: forty-one, forty-four, forty-six. And «zero-zero-twelve».
rad.lostPower: Power lost: the receiver went silent
rad.num2: «…zero, zero, twelve… zero, zero, twelve… repeat…»
rad.num3: «…don't look for those who walk on the ice toward the smoke… zero, zero, twelve…»
rad.sondeCalm: The sonde sent data: no storms expected soon
rad.sondeDrift: The next ice shift in ~{h} h. Cracks are marked on the ice map

stn.hintDamper: Damper in the flue: open means hotter and faster burning; closed means a quiet, long smoulder, but without a vent it means carbon monoxide.
stn.hintGen: Diesel generator: pull the cord (hold E). In the frost it won't start without warmth nearby. Gives light, radio power and the heater, without fumes. It is loud and heard from afar. The exhaust pipe gets buried in snow.
stn.hintGram: Gramophone: three records. While it plays, you rest faster and sleep better in the warmth, and Sever lies down nearby.
stn.hintHatch: Roof: clear the snow with a shovel before it breaks through; dig out the diesel pipe. Descent: the ladder, or simply step off the edge.
stn.hintHatchT: Roof: clear snow with a shovel
stn.hintKettle: Kettle on the stove: water and dry tea make hot tea. It warms from inside and keeps you from freezing.
stn.hintMed: First-aid kit: bandages and alcohol for frostbitten hands, feet and face. Supplies are limited.
stn.hintShutter: Shutters: close them at night, since glass loses a lot of heat. The rope is below.
stn.shClosed: Shutters closed: the window doesn't let heat out
stw.bellBear: The bear retreats from the ringing
stw.bellFar: The ringing faded into the dark. Nobody answered
stw.bellFox: A fox is creeping toward the sound
stw.cartHit: The mine cart knocked you off your feet!
stw.cartPush: Push the cart with your shoulder: it will roll on the rails. Downhill, it runs away
stw.hintBell: Bell: the ringing scares a bear off for a minute or two, but a fox comes to it too. Don't leave food in sight.
stw.hintBellT: Bell: the ringing scares the bear
stw.hintCart: Mine cart on the rails: push it while walking into it. To the west the rails run downhill: a cart that gets going will fly down the slope and hit everything in its path.
tech.blocks_d: Cut a 2×1 block from dense packed snow with a snow knife, 250–380 kg/m³. Loose snow (< 220) crumbles, and too dense (> 420) is heavy and sharp.
tech.brazier_d: An empty drum with the bottom knocked out and driftwood inside warms like a stove, but smokes.
tech.butchery_d: Butcher the seal right away, while it is warm: meat, fat, skin and sinew. Thread comes from the meat and sinew.
tech.cache_d: Six stones over the supplies: the arctic fox can't get in.
tech.cache_h: Someone has already lost food to a fox. Or you will.
tech.campfire_d: Two logs and lichen for kindling. In the wind the flame is weak: shield it with snow or a wall.
tech.cooking_d: Meat and fish are roasted over the fire; tea is brewed in the pot. Hot food warms you from inside for a long time.
tech.dry_mittens_d: Hands turn white first. Swap wet mittens for dry ones, dry them by the fire, and in a blizzard tuck your hands inside your coat.
tech.drying_d: Two poles and a rope: by the fire, wet clothes dry twice as fast.
tech.drying_h: A fire burned in the miners' hut and things dried there.
tech.expBrazier: made a brazier from a drum
tech.expCO: after the first headache from fumes
tech.fishing_d: A bone hook and sinew. Fish are caught at the hole or polynya, with bare fingers, which freeze.
tech.fishing_h: On the beach, by the bones, someone wrote down how to fish.
tech.harpoon_d: Bone, driftwood, rope and a piece of iron for the tip. Needed for a seal at the hole.
tech.harpoon_h: The keeper kept a log at the station. It says how to hunt on the ice.
tech.hides_d: A hide and lichen bed keeps cold from below; a hide flap closes the entrance.
tech.hides_h: In the underground hut someone cared about warm sleep.
tech.ice_chisel_d: Two iron bits and driftwood on a shaft. Cuts holes, breaks ice and reads its thickness.
tech.ice_chisel_h: The keeper wrote about ice and the barrels in the diesel shed.
tech.lamp_d: Soapstone (or tin with canvas), fat and a lichen wick. A fingernail-sized flame warms a closed snow house, but it needs a vent.
tech.lamp_h: Someone wintered here before you and knew how to keep warm in a snow house. Look for notes by the old cairn on the cape.
tech.mast_d: Three planks (or a bone) and two ropes: without the mast, the radio is just a box.
tech.mast_h: The keeper knew what happened to the radio. Check the house.
tech.parka_d: Three seal hides, two arctic foxes and a heavier thread, or a bear hide. The warmest clothing.
tech.parka_h: Somewhere in the ice, patterns for a fur parka are recorded.
tech.pot_d: The pot is made from tin. Snow and ice turn to water over the fire; ice gives twice as much water.
tech.rope_d: Canvas or sinew is twisted into rope.
tech.sewing_d: Mittens, kamiks and a hood: hide, fur and sinew. Fine work, since fingers lose feeling in the cold.
tech.sewing_h: The musher sewed by the big bones on the shore.
tech.sled_d: Four planks, two bones, straps: one man hauls the load of three.
tech.sled_h: The sled was built from ship timber.
tech.snares_d: A rope and a twig on the tundra by the lichen: a ptarmigan will get caught by itself while you're busy with something else.
tech.snares_h: One of the miners shared tips on traps in the hut.
tech.snow_roll_d: Fell in? Don't shake yourself off. Get out onto dry snow and roll: the powder draws water from the fur. Then to the fire.
tech.timber_d: The frozen mine roof rests on two props. Creaking is a warning: one prop is knocked out and the roof has already sagged. Don't touch the second, and don't stand under the gravel.
tech.torch_d: Driftwood, a drop of fat or diesel and a scrap of canvas: an hour of light and some warmth. Animals don't like it.
tech.torch_h: The mine is dark. Someone walked there with fire, and notes lie in the gallery.
tech.unknownTech: You don't know how to do this yet
tech.vault_d: Three rows of blocks, each one slightly inward (R for dome mode): the vault holds without beams. A flat roof will collapse under its own snow.
tech.vent_d: Head buzzing, sleepy: that's carbon monoxide. In a closed snow house with a fire, make a hole in the ceiling; the thinner the ceiling, the better the draught.

tools.noFlame: Nothing to light the torch with
touch.radialCap: Pick an item · tap outside to close
touch.rotateHint: SNOWCRAFT is played in landscape orientation
unstuck.hint: Stuck? Dig sideways or up with the shovel, or press U.
unstuck.out: You dug yourself out of the snow.
unstuck.shake: Snow buried you. You shook it off.
useA.bdNone: Nothing to treat: no frostbite, no scar
useA.bdTip: Bandage: stand with the frostbitten part of your body and use it. If there is alcohol in the bag, it is used to treat the wound first: heals twice as well.
useA.bmTip: Fat balm: rub on hands and face before going out in the cold. Frostbite progresses 40% slower for about two hours.
useA.bmUsed: Rubbed on hands and face: for two hours
useA.bpTip: Reinforced backpack: while in the bag, six extra slots and 20 more kg of load, but you sweat 20% more.
useA.bpUse: Backpack: six more slots and +20 kg, but you sweat more
useA.flFroze: The water in the flask froze! Put it in the bag (under the parka) or set it by the fire
useA.gBlind: Snow glare: it stings your eyes. Put on goggles or step into shade
useA.gBlind2: Snow blindness: you can barely see!
useA.gTip: Goggles: wear them on your face. Without them on a bright day the snow blinds you, and in a blizzard the drift hits your face.
useA.hwLit: The hand warmer glows: {h} h of warmth
useA.hwNeed: Need coal and a burning fire nearby
useA.hwOut: The hand warmer burned out: need new coal
useA.hwStatus: The hand warmer still burns for {h} h
useA.hwTip: Hand warmer: put coal in it and light it by a fire. While it burns and is in your bag, hands and face freeze more slowly, and hands warm up.
useA.pcTip: Belt pouch: while in the bag, three quick slots on the belt (keys 7, 8, 9).
useA.pcUse: Pouch on the belt: three quick slots (keys 7, 8, 9)
useA.skEmpty: Nothing to pour: need snow, ice, coal or lichen
useA.skTip: Sack: pour in loose items (snow, ice, coal, lichen), up to 12 pieces: half the weight. To use again: add more or dump out. Wet snow soaks your clothes.
useA.skWet: Wet snow in the sack soaked your clothes
useA.spDrink: It burns the throat, you feel hot... but it's a trick: the body is cooling
useA.spTip: Alcohol: for wounds and frostbite together with a bandage. If you drink it, you feel warm, but the body loses heat faster. This is how people freeze to death.
useA.thCooled: The thermos has cooled: there is still water, but it no longer warms
useA.thNoSource: Nothing to fill it with: need a hot kettle, a pot of warm water, or water and a fire nearby
useA.thSip: A hot sip: warmth spreads through you
useA.thSipCold: A cold sip: water, but no warmth
useA.thTip: Thermos: fill it with hot water or tea by a fire, kettle or pot (empty thermos + use). Three sips: they warm and quench, and the warmth lasts about six hours.
useB.binDark: Dark: only what's close is visible
useB.binTip: Binoculars: hold LMB and the camera looks twice as far. In moonlight, aurora or at twilight, animals are visible at long range.
useB.clNeedBoots: Ice cleats attach to footwear: first put on boots or felt boots
useB.clTip: Ice cleats: strap onto boots or felt boots. Press to strap on or take off.
useB.cmpTip: Compass: press for the next target (station, schooner, signal hill, smoke, marks). Hold 0.6 s to mark this spot.
useB.prBridge: On step {n} ahead: a snow bridge over a gap
useB.prGround: Ahead is not ice: ground or stone
useB.prHole: On step {n} ahead: a polynya, clear water
useB.prIce: Ice ahead {cm} cm: passable, but thin
useB.prThin: On step {n} ahead: ice {cm} cm, thin. Don't walk
useB.prTip: Probe pole: poke the snow in front of you. It shows ice thickness, polynyas and voids under the snow up to six steps ahead. Visible on the snow for three seconds.
useB.prVoid: On step {n} ahead: ice over a void
useB.smLit: Smoke flare burning: smoke visible from afar, three minutes
useB.smTip: Smoke flare: light it. Thick smoke for three minutes, visible from afar by day and at twilight. The icebreaker takes it as a signal.
useB.whNoDog: Sever isn't nearby, nobody to whistle for
useB.whTip: Whistle: blow it and Sever comes running and follows you. Hold it to let him wait in place.

weather.falling: Pressure is falling: a blizzard ({kind}) arrives in ~{h} h.
weather.hint: The wind shifts, the sky clouds over…
weather.rising: Pressure is rising: the blizzard is leaving.
